Claimant narrative
On the early morning of Tuesday, December 2, 2025, a severe winter storm brought heavy wet snowfall and freezing temperatures to my residence. The accumulated snow weight caused my porch roof to collapse, sending falling debris onto household contents stored underneath. My woven rattan armchair was heavily impact-damaged with a bent frame. All affected items are my private household furnishings kept for residential use.

To the Claims Department,
My name is SYN-Given-16 SYN-Family-42, and I am writing to formally report a loss under policy number PZ-PBI-000000043. I reside at 45 SYN-Street-45, SYN-City-05, KRP-11 01, SYN-Country.
On the morning of Wednesday, December 3, 2025, we woke up to discover that the outbuilding on our property had suffered a major structural failure. We had been in the middle of a severe winter storm with persistent heavy snowfall and freezing temperatures. By the time I stepped outside, the sheer weight of the accumulated snow had caused the roof to collapse completely.
I want to confirm that our regular residence — same living arrangement as always. We live here day-to-day, and there have been no changes to how we occupy the property.
The damage to the structure is extensive. The main wooden roof beams in the roof space completely buckled and fractured under the pressure. The collapse transferred a lot of force to the rest of the building. The brick wall on the south side bowed outward and developed large cracks. The steel roll-up door on the north entrance was struck by falling debris, leaving the frame and tracks bent and unusable. Inside the hallway, the drywall partition wall collapsed and became water-damaged from the meltwater. I also noticed that the concrete foundation around the base has developed cracks and settled slightly where the weight shifted.
When I first saw the extent of the destruction, I wasn't sure exactly where to begin. I stood there for a moment, feeling uncertain about the safest way to proceed. Eventually, I resolved to act immediately to prevent further issues. I went to work making the area safe below the affected structure, clearing the zone so no one would be in danger. After securing the site, I arranged for a professional assessment of the damage to understand the full scope.
I have preserved the damaged items in their current state and have taken photographs. I am fully prepared to allow your adjusters to inspect the property at their convenience.
Please advise on the claims process and any documentation you require.
SYN-Given-16 SYN-Family-42

OFFICIAL METEOROLOGICAL AND HYDROLOGICAL EVENT ASSESSMENT
Report Reference: NHMI-SYN-2025-1203-05A
Date of Issue: 2025-12-03
Observation Sector: SYN-City-05 Metropolitan Zone
Geospatial Coordinates: 45 SYN-Street-45, SYN-City-05, KRP-11 01, SYN-Country
Primary Monitoring Station: SYN-MET-05-A
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
This official document certifies the atmospheric and hydrometeorological conditions recorded on December 3, 2025. The assessment is derived from continuous telemetry data, automated weather station logs, and localized field sampling conducted by the National Hydrometeorological Institute. The data confirms the occurrence of a severe winter storm event characterized by intense precipitation, critical snow accumulation, and extreme static loading conditions.
SYNOPTIC OVERVIEW
A deep continental anticyclone interacted with a moisture-laden frontal system, generating a prolonged period of intense orographic and convective snowfall across the observation sector. Surface temperatures remained consistently sub-freezing throughout the event window, preventing melt cycles and facilitating rapid snowpack stratification. The atmospheric pressure gradient supported sustained wind patterns that contributed to asymmetric snow drift and localized load concentration on exposed structures.
PRIMARY METEOROLOGICAL MEASUREMENTS
The following parameters were recorded by Station SYN-MET-05-A and validated through ground-level verification during the critical event window:
- Air Temperature: Mean daily value of -7.4°C; minimum recorded -13.8°C at 04:15 local time.
- Precipitation Accumulation: 54.2 mm water equivalent recorded over a 20-hour window (01:00 to 21:00).
- Snowfall Depth: Peak accumulation of 52 cm measured at 07:30 local time.
- Snow Density Profile: In-situ sampling indicates a mean bulk density of 315 kg/m³, consistent with heavy, wet snow conditions.
- Wind Dynamics: Sustained winds averaging 9.5 m/s with peak gusts reaching 24.1 m/s from the northwest quadrant.
STRUCTURAL LOAD ANALYSIS
Based on the recorded depth and density parameters, the calculated static snow load at the time of peak accumulation was approximately 163.8 kg/m². This value significantly exceeds the standard design load thresholds typically applicable to auxiliary residential structures and outbuildings in this climatic zone. The temporal distribution of precipitation indicates a rapid loading rate exceeding 8.5 kg/m² per hour during the critical early-morning window, creating immediate physical stress on roofing systems.
SEVERITY CLASSIFICATION AND IMPACT ASSESSMENT
The event has been classified under Winter Storm Severity Level 3 (Critical Accumulation). The combination of high-density snowfall, sustained sub-zero temperatures, and rapid load accumulation created conditions physically sufficient to induce structural failure in non-reinforced roofing systems through gravitational snow weight alone. The recorded parameters establish a direct causal link between the meteorological event and the extreme mechanical stress applied to structures within the specified geospatial coordinates.
CERTIFICATION
The National Hydrometeorological Institute confirms that the recorded atmospheric and hydrometeorological data for December 3, 2025, directly support the physical mechanism of snow-weight-induced structural loading at the specified location. This report serves as the official technical record of the meteorological event.
Signed,
Dr. V. Koval, Senior Meteorological Analyst
National Hydrometeorological Institute, SYN-Country

Site Inspection Report
Inspector Name: SYN-Inspector-30703
Inspection Date: 2025-12-11
Location: 45 SYN-Street-45, SYN-City-05, KRP-11 01, SYN-Country
On the date of inspection, I arrived at the residential property located at 45 SYN-Street-45, SYN-City-05, KRP-11 01, SYN-Country. The weather conditions were cold and clear, consistent with the current winter season. The property is an occupied residential dwelling, and the claimant was present to guide the inspection. The primary objective was to assess the physical condition of the outbuilding following the loss event reported on 2025-12-03.
Upon initial approach, the severity of the structural failure was evident. The investigation confirms that the cause of loss is that snow weight caused the outbuilding roof to collapse. Visual inspection revealed no signs of pre-existing dilapidation, rot, or negligent maintenance; the structure appeared to be maintained in a reasonable state of repair prior to the severe winter storm. The collapse mechanism aligns with excessive vertical loading from accumulated snow and ice during the early morning of the incident.
Inside the Roof space, the Primary timber-truss roof framing system was found to be destroyed. The central load-bearing beams buckled and fractured inward under the vertical force of the accumulated snow and ice, resulting in a catastrophic loss of overhead structural support. The timber members are splintered and displaced, with no remaining capacity to bear load. As a direct consequence, the South-facing reinforced masonry exterior wall, located at the Exterior south wall, is heavily damaged. The wall panels bowed outward and developed extensive longitudinal stress fractures as the shifting roof loads transferred lateral pressure against the facade during the collapse.
At the North entrance, the Northern steel-framed roll-up access door assembly is heavily damaged. The header beam warped downward and the side tracks bent laterally due to direct impact with falling roof debris and displaced structural members, rendering the entryway inoperable. Within the Interior hallway, the Interior gypsum board partition wall system is moderately damaged. The drywall panels collapsed onto the floor and sustained saturation from meltwater runoff following the roof breach, resulting in compromised integrity. Finally, at the Exterior foundation, the Perimeter concrete foundation footing is lightly damaged. Several sections developed hairline cracks and minor settlement where displaced earth and concentrated structural weight pressed against the footing during the event.
Safety measures were implemented to secure the area below the affected structure. The damage is strictly limited to the building structure and is consistent with the reported mechanism of snow weight causing the outbuilding roof to collapse.
